clauses.current_legal_basis: The original text of EO 11545 (35 FR 11161) states no end for this clause, and no held later order, statute text or search result revokes or supersedes it (amendments are recorded as later events, not ends). The three selected machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no revocation or supersession of EO 11545. The clause therefore continues on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The clause is the whole order: the Defense Distinguished Service Medal is established for award by the Secretary of Defense for exceptionally meritorious service in a duty of great responsibility with the listed defense and joint activities, with design and regulations approved by the Secretary of Defense, a precedence rule, one medal with devices, and posthumous award. EO 14085 section 6 (87 FR 60541, effective on signing October 3, 2022, as the order states no other effective date) strikes military officer in section 1 and inserts member of the Armed Forces of the United States, and strikes he in section 2 and inserts the Secretary. Before: award to a military officer, under regulations he prescribes; after: award to a member of the Armed Forces under regulations the Secretary prescribes. The eligible class was widened but the medal and its award authority continue. Nothing held ends the clause.

research_rationale:
EO 11545 (signed July 9, 1970; 35 FR 11161, Federal Register issue of July 11, 1970) establishes the Defense Distinguished Service Medal. I read the complete held Federal Register text (a machine text layer of the printed page): an authority paragraph and four sections (establishment and eligibility; design, regulations and precedence; one medal with devices; posthumous award). The held text has a few dropped words in section 4 and a misspelled title, so I quote nothing from those lines. The dossier inventory is one clause covering the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. The order has no end date or ending condition and revokes nothing. EO 14085 (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541), section 6, amends it: section 1 is amended by striking military officer and inserting member of the Armed Forces of the United States, and section 2 by striking he and inserting the Secretary. That is a later event on a continuing clause, recorded with its text before and after in the clause reason, not an end. The held-text number search also finds only the 1989 OFR codification snapshot (historical editorial, not a current basis) and EO 14085. The U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1125 with no ending statement (a machine pointer; held statutory text is not relied on). The three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record only the EO 14085 amendment and no revocation or supersession. The clause is operative as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.
